title: World's Lightest Solid!
speaker: Veritasium
zh: 【Veritasium】世界上最輕的固體！（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: This is aerogel. The world's lightest, that is least dense, solid.
cues.en: This is aerogel. The world's lightest, that is least dense, solid.
cues.zh: 這是氣凝膠 世界上最輕的固體

cues.text: This piece has a mass of just 1.22 grams.
cues.en: This piece has a mass of just 1.22 grams.
cues.zh: 這一塊氣凝膠的質量 只有1.22公克

cues.text: That is only a few times the mass of the same volume of air, which kind of makes sense because it is
cues.en: That is only a few times the mass of the same volume of air, which kind of makes sense because it is
cues.zh: 他的質量只有同體積空氣的數倍而已 這其實不難理解 因為它有99.8%的質量是空氣本身的質量

cues.text: 99.8% air. In fact, some aerogels are so light that if you removed all the air from them,
cues.en: 99.8% air. In fact, some aerogels are so light that if you removed all the air from them,
cues.zh: 這其實不難理解 因為它有99.8%的質量是空氣本身的質量 事實上，有些氣凝膠非常輕 如果把空氣從中移除，

cues.text: they would be less dense than air. I have long been fascinated by aerogel
cues.en: they would be less dense than air. I have long been fascinated by aerogel
cues.zh: 如果把空氣從中移除， 它的密度會比空氣還小 我一直對氣凝膠很著迷

cues.text: so I actually flew out to Aerogel Technologies in Boston to find out why was aerogel invented. How is it made?
cues.en: so I actually flew out to Aerogel Technologies in Boston to find out why was aerogel invented. How is it made?
cues.zh: 我一直對氣凝膠很著迷 所以我飛到位於波士頓的氣凝膠科技公司去了解 為何會發明氣凝膠 它是如何生產的

cues.text: Why is it such a good thermal insulator and what is it used for?
cues.en: Why is it such a good thermal insulator and what is it used for?
cues.zh: 它是如何生產的 為什麼它是很好的隔熱材料 以及它的用途為何?

cues.text: Okay, we are going to try an experiment to demonstrate the insulating power of aerogel so over here we have
cues.en: Okay, we are going to try an experiment to demonstrate the insulating power of aerogel so over here we have
cues.zh: 以及它的用途為何? 好的 我們將嘗試進行實驗以證明氣凝膠的絕緣能力 因此，在這邊有兩組對照組

cues.text: two setups: one with a glass petri dish, and the other one with aerogel on top.
cues.en: two setups: one with a glass petri dish, and the other one with aerogel on top.
cues.zh: 因此，在這邊有兩組對照組 一種是放玻璃培養皿在上面 另外一種是放氣凝膠在上面

cues.text: Both are made of silica, but with very different physical structures.
cues.en: Both are made of silica, but with very different physical structures.
cues.zh: 一種是放玻璃培養皿在上面 另外一種是放氣凝膠在上面 兩者均由二氧化矽製成，但物理結構差異很大。

cues.text: We're gonna see how long it takes to melt these chocolate bunnies with a Bunsen burner.
cues.en: We're gonna see how long it takes to melt these chocolate bunnies with a Bunsen burner.
cues.zh: 兩者均由二氧化矽製成，但物理結構差異很大。 我們將看到用本生燈 將這些巧克力兔子融化需要多長時間。

cues.text: Now to have a look at this experiment, we have a FLIR T1020 which can see temperatures up to 2,000 degrees Celsius.
cues.en: Now to have a look at this experiment, we have a FLIR T1020 which can see temperatures up to 2,000 degrees Celsius.
cues.zh: 現在來看這個實驗我們有一臺FLIR T1020 它可以看到高達2,000攝氏度的溫度。

cues.text: Looks like it's getting pretty hot.
cues.en: Looks like it's getting pretty hot.
cues.zh: 它可以看到高達2,000攝氏度的溫度。

cues.text: Yeah, you can see that the glass is getting really hot already. And after just a minute:
cues.en: Yeah, you can see that the glass is getting really hot already. And after just a minute:
cues.zh: 是的，您可以看到玻璃已經開始真正變熱 一分鐘後 玻璃開始冒煙

cues.text: It's starting to smoke. Okay.
cues.en: It's starting to smoke. Okay.
cues.zh: 玻璃開始冒煙 好喔 wwwww

cues.text: It's definitely melting and smoking.
cues.en: It's definitely melting and smoking.
cues.zh: 巧克力開始融化和冒煙

cues.text: Oh, yeah, here we go. I would say that's phase change.
cues.en: Oh, yeah, here we go. I would say that's phase change.
cues.zh: 哇~讓我們看看 我會說他已經開始變形了

cues.text: We've got a liquid chocolate situation. We have some smoking bunny. Over here,
cues.en: We've got a liquid chocolate situation. We have some smoking bunny. Over here,
cues.zh: 我會說他已經開始變形了 我們看到了 巧克力變成液態，還有冒煙的兔子 在這邊兔子實際上有點融化了 看上去也有點向側面傾斜

cues.text: the bunny is actually sort of melting over, and look, there, it's sort of tilting to the side.
cues.en: the bunny is actually sort of melting over, and look, there, it's sort of tilting to the side.
cues.zh: 在這邊兔子實際上有點融化了 看上去也有點向側面傾斜

cues.text: Alright, I think we're going to call that a melt.
cues.en: Alright, I think we're going to call that a melt.
cues.zh: 在這邊兔子實際上有點融化了 看上去也有點向側面傾斜 好吧，我想我們稱其為融化

cues.text: What is that? Oh!
cues.en: What is that? Oh!
cues.zh: 發生什麼?

cues.text: On cue, on cue.
cues.en: On cue, on cue.
cues.zh: 剛剛好

cues.text: I would say that is material fail.
cues.en: I would say that is material fail.
cues.zh: 我會說這是實質上的失敗

cues.text: Not only did the bunny melt quickly, the petri dish cracked under the thermal expansion.
cues.en: Not only did the bunny melt quickly, the petri dish cracked under the thermal expansion.
cues.zh: 我會說這是實質上的失敗 兔子不僅迅速融化 而且在熱膨脹下培養皿也破裂了

cues.text: Wanna pop it in?
cues.en: Wanna pop it in?
cues.zh: 現在，來試試看氣凝膠

cues.text: So now let's try the aerogel.
cues.en: So now let's try the aerogel.
cues.zh: 現在，來試試看氣凝膠

cues.text: So how is aerogel invented back in?
cues.en: So how is aerogel invented back in?
cues.zh: 所以氣凝膠是怎麼被發明的呢? 在1931年

cues.text: Back in 1931, a guy named Professor Samuel Kistler had a bet with his colleague Charles Learned.
cues.en: Back in 1931, a guy named Professor Samuel Kistler had a bet with his colleague Charles Learned.
cues.zh: 在1931年 一個名叫塞繆爾·基斯勒（Samuel Kistler）教授的傢伙 就與他的同事查爾斯·勒尼德（Charles Learned）打賭。 賭注都是果凍

cues.text: Now the bet revolved around jellies, like peanut-butter-and-jelly jellies.
cues.en: Now the bet revolved around jellies, like peanut-butter-and-jelly jellies.
cues.zh: 賭注都是果凍 例如花生凍和果凍

cues.text: Now the thing about jellies is they are actually a combination of liquids and solids.
cues.en: Now the thing about jellies is they are actually a combination of liquids and solids.
cues.zh: 例如花生凍和果凍 果凍實際上是液體和固體的結合

cues.text: I mean, they're mostly liquid, but it's embedded within this 3D solid structure.
cues.en: I mean, they're mostly liquid, but it's embedded within this 3D solid structure.
cues.zh: 我的意思是 他們幾乎是液態的 但實際上卻充滿了3D實體結構

cues.text: So if you think of a gel, like jello, has a skeleton with nano-sized pores that gives it its rigidity,
cues.en: So if you think of a gel, like jello, has a skeleton with nano-sized pores that gives it its rigidity,
cues.zh: 但實際上卻充滿了3D實體結構 所以如果你想到凝膠，像是果凍 它的骨架都有奈米級的空隙 使其具有一點剛性

cues.text: and then that's about 1% of the gel.
cues.en: and then that's about 1% of the gel.
cues.zh: 它的骨架都有奈米級的空隙 使其具有一點剛性 其大約佔凝膠體積的1% 所以賭注是這樣的

cues.text: So the bet was this: Could you remove the liquid from the jelly?
cues.en: So the bet was this: Could you remove the liquid from the jelly?
cues.zh: 所以賭注是這樣的 你能從果凍中清除液體嗎?

cues.text: Without affecting the solid structure? I mean, if you just evaporate the liquid out, well,
cues.en: Without affecting the solid structure? I mean, if you just evaporate the liquid out, well,
cues.zh: 並且不影響實體結構 我的意思是 如果你只是將液體蒸發掉 固體結構就會收縮

cues.text: then the solid structure shrinks, because as you remove liquid molecules, they pull on each other,
cues.en: then the solid structure shrinks, because as you remove liquid molecules, they pull on each other,
cues.zh: 固體結構就會收縮 因為當你移除液體分子時 他們會互相拉扯 他們拉動周圍的堅固結構 從內部讓其坍塌

cues.text: and they pull on the solid structure around them, basically crumpling it from the inside.
cues.en: and they pull on the solid structure around them, basically crumpling it from the inside.
cues.zh: 他們拉動周圍的堅固結構 從內部讓其坍塌

cues.text: Now Samuel Kistler solved this problem in two ways.
cues.en: Now Samuel Kistler solved this problem in two ways.
cues.zh: 現在塞繆爾·奇斯勒以兩種方式解決了這個問題

cues.text: First, he realized you could replace one liquid with another
cues.en: First, he realized you could replace one liquid with another
cues.zh: 首先，他意識到 你可以用另一種液體替代果凍內原本的液體

cues.text: inside the jelly just by washing it thoroughly. So you could swap out, say,
cues.en: inside the jelly just by washing it thoroughly. So you could swap out, say,
cues.zh: 你可以用另一種液體替代果凍內原本的液體 所以你可以換掉 像是水替換酒精

cues.text: water, for alcohol. And then, if you take the jelly and put it in a high-pressure vessel called a autoclave,
cues.en: water, for alcohol. And then, if you take the jelly and put it in a high-pressure vessel called a autoclave,
cues.zh: 像是水替換酒精 然後 如果你將果凍放入高壓鍋 將其加熱到被稱為液體臨界點的高溫高壓點

cues.text: By heating it to the high-temperature, high-pressure point called the critical point of the liquid,
cues.en: By heating it to the high-temperature, high-pressure point called the critical point of the liquid,
cues.zh: 將其加熱到被稱為液體臨界點的高溫高壓點

cues.text: that liquid transformed into a semi-liquid, semi-gas called a supercritical fluid.
cues.en: that liquid transformed into a semi-liquid, semi-gas called a supercritical fluid.
cues.zh: 將其加熱到被稱為液體臨界點的高溫高壓點 該液體將會轉化為半液體、半氣體的形式 被稱為「超臨界流體」

cues.text: At this point, there is no longer a distinction between liquid and gas.
cues.en: At this point, there is no longer a distinction between liquid and gas.
cues.zh: 到這一步 氣體和液體之間將不再有明顯區別

cues.text: Those molecules are no longer pulling on each other.
cues.en: Those molecules are no longer pulling on each other.
cues.zh: 到這一步 氣體和液體之間將不再有明顯區別 這些分子將不再相互吸引 接著你再對容器開始減壓，就將只會剩下固體結構

cues.text: So once you've depressurized the vessel, that solid skeleton, that 1% of the mass of the gel, is left behind
cues.en: So once you've depressurized the vessel, that solid skeleton, that 1% of the mass of the gel, is left behind
cues.zh: 接著你再對容器開始減壓，就將只會剩下固體結構 它的質量將只剩下原本的1% 形狀完好無損

cues.text: intact, except for where there was liquid in the pores before is now gas,
cues.en: intact, except for where there was liquid in the pores before is now gas,
cues.zh: 形狀完好無損 除了原本是液體的地方現在是氣體 這個固體架構，即奈米級多孔固體 就是我們說的氣凝膠

cues.text: and that solid skeleton, that nanoporous solid is what we call aerogel.
cues.en: and that solid skeleton, that nanoporous solid is what we call aerogel.
cues.zh: 這個固體架構，即奈米級多孔固體 就是我們說的氣凝膠

cues.text: Kistler published his findings in Nature in 1931.
cues.en: Kistler published his findings in Nature in 1931.
cues.zh: 基斯勒在1931年在《自然》雜誌上發表了他的發現

cues.text: It is getting pretty hot as you can see through the thermal camera.
cues.en: It is getting pretty hot as you can see through the thermal camera.
cues.zh: 火焰的溫度越來越熱 正如你從熱像儀所看到的

cues.text: But coming up on three minutes, there's still no sign of melted chocolate.
cues.en: But coming up on three minutes, there's still no sign of melted chocolate.
cues.zh: 但是三分鐘過後 巧克力仍然沒有融化的跡象

cues.text: So we're gonna pull out a thermocouple and just check the temperature underneath the bunny.
cues.en: So we're gonna pull out a thermocouple and just check the temperature underneath the bunny.
cues.zh: 因此，我們要將溫度感應器移開 並確認兔子下方的溫度

cues.text: Like, underneath the aerogel, and see what, what the flame temperature is.
cues.en: Like, underneath the aerogel, and see what, what the flame temperature is.
cues.zh: 像是氣凝膠下方的火焰溫度是幾度

cues.text: You can kind of see that, that parts of the bunny are getting hot, but it's not the bottom of the bunny,
cues.en: You can kind of see that, that parts of the bunny are getting hot, but it's not the bottom of the bunny,
cues.zh: 像是氣凝膠下方的火焰溫度是幾度 你可以看到兔子的周圍都在變熱 但都不是因為兔子底部傳上來的

cues.text: It's all the, around the bunny.
cues.en: It's all the, around the bunny.
cues.zh: 但都不是因為兔子底部傳上來的 溫度全部都在兔子周圍

cues.text: Exactly. That convective heat is moving up and around the aerogel,
cues.en: Exactly. That convective heat is moving up and around the aerogel,
cues.zh: 溫度全部都在兔子周圍 沒錯! 熱對流都透過氣凝膠周圍向上移動

cues.text: So you can see the thing is getting red hot. And by four minutes, the bunny is looking a little soft.
cues.en: So you can see the thing is getting red hot. And by four minutes, the bunny is looking a little soft.
cues.zh: 沒錯! 熱對流都透過氣凝膠周圍向上移動 你可以看到鐵絲已經被燒紅了 四分鐘後，兔子看上去有點融化的跡象

cues.text: Still pretty good though, considering how easy it is to melt chocolate.
cues.en: Still pretty good though, considering how easy it is to melt chocolate.
cues.zh: 四分鐘後，兔子看上去有點融化的跡象 考慮到巧克力很容易融化 它目前的狀態已經很不錯了

cues.text: Can I put my finger here?
cues.en: Can I put my finger here?
cues.zh: 我可以把手指放這邊嗎?

cues.text: Be careful.
cues.en: Be careful.
cues.zh: 小心一點

cues.text: It's not that it's hot, it's that it's brittle. Right.
cues.en: It's not that it's hot, it's that it's brittle. Right.
cues.zh: 不是因為它很燙，是因為它很脆弱 沒錯

cues.text: But yeah, totally cool to touch, right? It is, it is just warm to the touch.
cues.en: But yeah, totally cool to touch, right? It is, it is just warm to the touch.
cues.zh: 但是觸感很酷對吧~ 是的，摸起來很溫暖

cues.text: He made aerogels out of all sorts of things.
cues.en: He made aerogels out of all sorts of things.
cues.zh: 是的，摸起來很溫暖 他把各種各樣的東西做成氣凝膠

cues.text: He made them out of eggs. He made them out of rubber, out of nitrocellulose.
cues.en: He made them out of eggs. He made them out of rubber, out of nitrocellulose.
cues.zh: 他把各種各樣的東西做成氣凝膠 他用雞蛋做過，也用橡膠做過，還有硝化纖維

cues.text: And, included in there was silica. Actually right here on the table, I have some examples of some silica gels.
cues.en: And, included in there was silica. Actually right here on the table, I have some examples of some silica gels.
cues.zh: 當然他們都是由二氧化矽所組成 事實上，在這張桌上我有準備一些矽膠製品

cues.text: This is a, a wet silica gel It's kind of rubbery so I can just, you know, carve out a piece.
cues.en: This is a, a wet silica gel It's kind of rubbery so I can just, you know, carve out a piece.
cues.zh: 事實上，在這張桌上我有準備一些矽膠製品 這是一個矽膠凍 這有點像橡膠，所以我可以這樣做 你懂的，切出一塊 他整體的97%，也就是空隙內充滿了酒精

cues.text: It is 97% alcohol inside of its pores.
cues.en: It is 97% alcohol inside of its pores.
cues.zh: 他整體的97%，也就是空隙內充滿了酒精

cues.text: And then the remaining 3% solid is amorphous silica. Just--
cues.en: And then the remaining 3% solid is amorphous silica. Just--
cues.zh: 剩餘的3%固體則是無定型的二氧化矽

cues.text: Can I touch it? Yeah, absolutely. It's kind of rubbery. Not that strong.
cues.en: Can I touch it? Yeah, absolutely. It's kind of rubbery. Not that strong.
cues.zh: 剩餘的3%固體則是無定型的二氧化矽 我可以碰他嗎? 當然可以! 它有點像橡膠，沒這麼硬

cues.text: So was I cracking it there or was it already kinda cracked?
cues.en: So was I cracking it there or was it already kinda cracked?
cues.zh: 我不小心弄碎它了嗎? 還是它原本就已經碎了?

cues.text: Yeah, you just, no-- Oh whoa, it's very easy to break. Very crumbly.
cues.en: Yeah, you just, no-- Oh whoa, it's very easy to break. Very crumbly.
cues.zh: 我不小心弄碎它了嗎? 還是它原本就已經碎了? 它非常容易碎掉，非常脆弱

cues.text: The next step is to replace the alcohol in the gel with liquid carbon dioxide.
cues.en: The next step is to replace the alcohol in the gel with liquid carbon dioxide.
cues.zh: 下一步是用液態二氧化碳替代凝膠中的酒精 我們即將看到液態的CO₂

cues.text: We're about to see liquid CO₂.
cues.en: We're about to see liquid CO₂.
cues.zh: 我們即將看到液態的CO₂

cues.text: Liquid CO₂ has the advantage of being non-flammable, plus it's got a low critical temperature.
cues.en: Liquid CO₂ has the advantage of being non-flammable, plus it's got a low critical temperature.
cues.zh: 我們即將看到液態的CO₂ 液態的CO₂具有不可燃的優點，並且擁有很低的臨界溫度

cues.text: Open it up, and-- Yeah, I see it flooding in there.
cues.en: Open it up, and-- Yeah, I see it flooding in there.
cues.zh: 液態的CO₂具有不可燃的優點，並且擁有很低的臨界溫度 開啟它 我看到它在溢流

cues.text: Yeah, it's flooding in. There it goes. Just another solvent.
cues.en: Yeah, it's flooding in. There it goes. Just another solvent.
cues.zh: 開啟它 我看到它在溢流 是的，它在溢流，就是這樣 它只是另一種溶劑

cues.text: You can clearly see that it's so much cooler on top.
cues.en: You can clearly see that it's so much cooler on top.
cues.zh: 你可以清楚的看到 它的頂部很涼爽

cues.text: What temperature is it on the bottom? We're at 600 right now?
cues.en: What temperature is it on the bottom? We're at 600 right now?
cues.zh: 它底部的溫度是多少? 現在有600多度了

cues.text: 600 degrees Celsius. 600 degrees Celsius, that's 1250 Fahrenheit right now.
cues.en: 600 degrees Celsius. 600 degrees Celsius, that's 1250 Fahrenheit right now.
cues.zh: 600攝氏度 即代表現在有1250華氏度

cues.text: Notice where the bunny is melting.
cues.en: Notice where the bunny is melting.
cues.zh: 即代表現在有1250華氏度 注意一下兔子哪邊融化了

cues.text: It's melting right on that edge where the heat's, like, the flame is kind of crawling up and over. - So, yeah, that's
cues.en: It's melting right on that edge where the heat's, like, the flame is kind of crawling up and over. - So, yeah, that's

cues.text: Oh!
cues.en: Oh!
cues.zh: 兔子倒了

cues.en: Bunny down!
